crop.notes: The Allen item 'Three in a Row' is complete. The crop also takes in the unrelated item below it, 'Went Up for Fifteen Years' (John Emory, highway robbery).

ocr.notes: Minor errors ('Jucik Looney', 'opeved', 'ottriends'); the transcript also includes the unrelated Emory item.

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that Tom Allen, the ex-champion pugilist, had opened a saloon on Market Street between Sixth and Seventh, next door to Tom Kelly's and near Jack Looney's; the three were the best of friends.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads THE REPUBLICAN: ST. LOUIS, SUNDAY MORNING, MARCH 4, 1883, page 16. The paper was then the (Missouri) Republican, not yet the St. Louis Republic.

facts.fact: Allen opened a saloon on Market Street between Sixth and Seventh, next door to Tom Kelly's saloon, which was two doors from Jack Looney's; the three were described as the best of friends
places: Market Street between Sixth and Seventh, St. Louis

notes: This dates the opening of Allen's Market Street saloon to about early March 1883 (compare the unnumbered index item on his December 1882 return to St. Louis to set up a saloon with John C. Gropper).
